My other apps

The ones people download most, and a few I'm proudest of.

CallShield · Android · ⭐90 · 4,000+ downloads
Blocks spam calls and flags spam texts with an on-device model and a signed database of 51,000+ numbers. No API keys and no subscription.

OpenLumen · Android · ⭐21 · 1,400+ downloads
A screen color filter that changes the display itself instead of painting a layer on top. Warm the screen on a schedule or fix a panel's color cast, fully offline.

SwiftFloris · Android · ⭐40 · 1,300+ downloads
A SwiftKey-style keyboard built on FlorisBoard, with no internet permission at all. Import your SwiftKey or Gboard dictionary and it all stays on your phone.

Rclone Browser NG · Windows, macOS, Linux · ⭐23
A desktop app for rclone that picks up where the abandoned RcloneBrowser left off. Browse any remote, encrypted ones included, while transfers run in the background.

AppManagerNG · Android · ⭐213 · 13,000+ downloads
See every app on your phone and what it can reach. Freeze or remove the bloat and back up the rest, with or without root.

SnapCrop · Android · ⭐18
Catches each screenshot as you take it and opens it in an editor with the status and nav bars already cropped off. Scrolling capture and automatic redaction of sensitive text are free.

HushFacebook Web · Browser · ⭐55 · 3,000+ downloads
Takes ads and suggested posts out of Facebook in a desktop browser, and adds downloads and privacy switches. Runs as a userscript or a Chrome extension.

ZeusWatch · Android · ⭐17 · 1,300+ downloads
Weather with a second opinion. Put forecast providers side by side to see where the models disagree, then keep the sources you trust. No account needed.

AlarmClockXtreme · Android · ⭐55 · 2,000+ downloads
An alarm clock for heavy sleepers. Exact scheduling and 30 dismiss challenges get you up and keep you up, with no ads and no account.

OpenNetLimit · Windows · ⭐30 · 1,100+ downloads
See which apps are using your connection, then cap the ones that hog it. Per-app limits, traffic history, quotas and schedules on Windows.

Pick your problem

Start from the job you need done.

Hi there 👋 — I'm Steven Zhao

Independent developer & DevOps engineer focused on data engineering. I build and maintain open source tools that move data across RDBMS, NoSQL, and big data systems — most notably Addax, a widely used ETL tool that started as a fork of Alibaba DataX.

🔥 Featured Project

Addax — a fast, versatile ETL tool connecting 20+ databases and data sources, engineered for reliable bulk data transfer and easy plugin extension.

  • Reader/Writer plugin architecture: add a new data source without touching the core engine
  • Rich RDBMS support (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, ClickHouse, ...) plus NoSQL and big data sources (HBase, MongoDB, Kafka, HDFS, ...)
  • Optimized for large-scale batch jobs: stable, observable, actively maintained

🧰 What I Work With

Java and Python day-to-day, with Vue for the occasional web frontend, running on Kubernetes and friends.

👋 Hey there, I'm Matheus Oliveira!




💫 About Me

Most Java developers know Quarkus. Few understand the Quarkus Way.

The Quarkus Way is more than using a framework. It is a shift in how you think about building Java applications: startup in milliseconds, minimal memory footprint, compile-time optimization, and developer joy through live reload. When you master this approach, you stop building Java apps the old way and start building software that is truly cloud native.

I help professional Java developers make that shift.

🔹 Open Source Contributions Across the Quarkus Ecosystem

  • Quarkus LangChain4j — Built the @OnThinking annotation for reasoning output handlers, added named embedding store support across six databases (pgvector, Chroma, Milvus, Neo4j, Weaviate, Qdrant), introduced the Oracle embedding store extension, implemented audio transcription for OpenAI, added support for additional model options in Ollama, and enabled named OIDC clients in OidcClientMcpAuthProvider.
  • Quarkus Roq & Qute Web — Enhanced the Roq Editor with SSH agent integration for secure git sync, and added GFM alert block support to the Qute Web markdown plugin.
  • pt.quarkus.io — As maintainer of the Brazilian Portuguese translation, I fixed broken guides after upstream Web Components migration, improved contributor onboarding with CONTRIBUTING.md, and translated key documentation.
  • Quarkus Core — Contributed Javadoc for build item documentation (ApplicationInfoBuildItem, AdditionalClassLoaderResourcesBuildItem).

🔹 Production Experience at Scale

AWS Certified and focused on cloud-native architectures. As a Software Engineer at BMW Group TechWorks Brasil powered by act digital, I build cloud-native applications with Quarkus, Angular, and AWS. My broader background includes Spring Boot, messaging (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS/SNS), and CI/CD automation.

🔹 From Music to Code

My path to software engineering was unconventional. Before code, I spent seven years as a music teacher, developing the analytical ear and collaborative discipline that now drive my work in agile teams. That background taught me something valuable: the best engineers, like the best musicians, are the ones who listen before they play.

If you are building with Quarkus, contributing to the ecosystem, or looking for someone who lives the Quarkus Way, let's connect.

📧 Get in touch: hi@omatheusmesmo.dev

📝 Latest Blog Posts

Writing about Java, cloud-native architectures, and open source

  • Oracle Cloud on localhost with floci-oci
    Hands-on guide to floci-oci 0.7.0, the free open source Oracle Cloud Infrastructure emulator. Build a Quarkus expense receipts service on OCI Database with PostgreSQL (password from a Vault secret, TLS verify-full), Object Storage pre-authenticated uploads, Queue with a dead-letter queue and KMS envelope encryption. Test it with Testcontainers, drive it from the unmodified OCI CLI and provision it with Terraform and OpenTofu, with a zero drift plan.

  • IBM Bob and the bet on repeatable modernization
    IBM Bob in 2026: the V2 architecture, the Agent, Plan and Ask modes, model routing, the Premium Packages for Java, IBM i and IBM Z, Bobcoin pricing, how it compares with Claude Code and Codex, and how to adopt the agent in a team with permissions and cost control.

  • Inside the Quarkus reactive core, part 4: reactive or virtual threads in Quarkus 4
    Reactive or virtual threads in Quarkus 4: why event loops are not carriers, what Java 21, Jackson 3, Vert.x 5 and Netty 4.2 change, Little's law applied to the Quarkus default pools, an open-model benchmark of the three models on Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1 and 3.40.1, why reactive and virtual threads collapse past the REST Client connection pool while workers hold, a pinning audit per integration and a decision table.

  • Inside the Quarkus reactive core, part 3: a Uni is a recipe, not a result
    Mutiny explained through tests: a Uni is a lazy recipe, the invoke that silently drops a Uni, retry as resubscription, why Mutiny does not schedule anything except with emitOn and runSubscriptionOn, why combine does not parallelize, failures as terminal events, demand and back-pressure, and the two TimeoutExceptions that look alike.

  • Inside the Quarkus reactive core, part 2: who runs your code
    How Quarkus REST, Reactive Messaging and the Scheduler choose between the event loop, a worker and a virtual thread: the signature rule decided at build time, the annotations that override it, the @Transactional rule the code dropped, @RunOnVirtualThread on a Uni, which thread runs your filters and where a ThreadLocal stops working.
